A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TextMaster and retain identifiable method components and appendix examples. All pages, including equations, tables, figures and supplementary material, are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original quantitative comparisons, component ablations and qualitative text-editing results in Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–8.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results, revised component ablations, external-style editing examples and supplementary text-rendering results.

M1.justification: V2 adds In-Context Reference: a segmented reference character is placed in the input image for self-attention, with reference-character erasure during training to discourage glyph copying. It also describes restricting style-adapter attention to editing regions. These extend the procedure beyond v1's DINOv2 feature subtraction and IP-Adapter injection; the character-separated encoder itself is retained.

E1.justification: V2 adds 100,000 artistic-style posters for training, a custom TextMaster evaluation dataset, and external-reference style transfer and general text-rendering scenarios (Figures 1 and 9). Dedicated TextSeg and LAION-OCR quantitative evaluations disappear. Chinese/English editing, ICDAR13, AnyText examples and the LAION/Wukong multi-line appendix remain represented.

E2.justification: V1 Table 1 evaluates MOSTEL, SD-Inpainting, DiffSTE, TextDiffuser and UdiffText, with AnyText compared qualitatively. V2 Table 1 instead evaluates SDXL, FLUX, TextDiffuser2, AnyText-v1.1, AnyText2 and TextCtrl. Thus comparator membership changes substantially, including on the retained ICDAR13 benchmark.

E3.justification: The reported two-epoch plus three-epoch training schedule becomes five epochs on AnyWord-3M followed by staged poster/style training. V2's replacement evaluations explicitly separate random-text accuracy from original-text style similarity, introduce NED, and remove the manual Average Availability measure and separate reconstruction/editing columns. These are substantial changes in training and evaluation design.

E4.justification: V1 Table 2 separately tests glyph injection, glyph-feature loss, pixel loss and attention loss for English and Chinese. V2 replaces this with cumulative tests of character-separated encoding, combined perceptual loss, IoU loss, In-Context Reference and Style-Adapter. This adds direct tests of previously unablated style components while removing language-separated and individual perceptual-loss analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The 500-image evaluations concern sample size, not repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Both quantitative tables are replaced, and new qualitative results are added. For example, v1 reports ICDAR13 editing accuracy of 86.0%, whereas v2 reports Acc 0.9100 under its revised protocol; this does not establish a same-setting gain. Rankings also differ: v2 gives TextCtrl better English AnyText FID and LPIPS than TextMaster, despite the accompanying all-metrics superiority claim.

T1.justification: V2 adds an explicit reconstruction expression and weighted total objective (Eq. 12). Its perceptual-loss formula also changes from two squared L2 terms in v1 to an unsquared pixel norm in Eq. 4, despite retaining the MSE description; whether this is intentional is unclear. The attention/CIoU mathematics remains, and neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 makes external-reference style injection and real-image glyph/style disentanglement through Style-Adapter plus In-Context Reference central contributions. It drops v1's explicit first-model claim for multi-line editing and its blanket assertion that prior methods lack controllable style transfer. Accurate multilingual editing, adaptive layout and state-of-the-art performance remain core claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of contextual color contamination, reference-glyph copying and style guidance improving glyph accuracy. It interprets TextCtrl's reconstruction advantage as retention of original text and newly states an inability to edit non-continuous multi-line text simultaneously. These substantially expand mechanism explanations and applicability boundaries beyond v1.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents four H20 GPUs, 1024 training resolution, Kolors IPA initialization, loss weights 0.1/0.05, a nine-character crop threshold and staged parameter freezing. Conversely, v1's explicit 1.0–1.3 mask-expansion range and several training-subset counts are omitted. These materially change reproducibility information; newly specified crop and hardware details alone do not establish changed implementation.

R1.justification: The research positioning is substantially rewritten around modern glyph and style control, adding discussion of TextDiffuser-2, Glyph-ByT5 variants, AnyText2, Fonts and TextCtrl. V2 acknowledges existing style-control approaches and distinguishes its real-image disentanglement from synthetic-font training and inversion methods, replacing v1's broader absence-of-prior-style-control premise.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Methods are reorganized into numbered glyph/style subsections with new preliminaries, and supplementary captions become a structured appendix with dedicated discussions. The title, author information and terminology also change.

P2.justification: Figures 1–4 are substantially revised, including an In-Context branch in the architecture diagram. Both tables are rebuilt, and new comparison/rendering panels appear in Figures 6, 9 and 10. The retained tiny-font example moves from Figure 6 to Figure 5, while the earlier full-page supplementary Figures 7–8 are compressed into the expanded appendix.

improvement.justification: V2 better supports its central style-control contribution through direct component ablations, updated comparisons, more implementation detail and a concrete applicability limitation. These gains outweigh the loss of some diagnostic analyses, but inconsistencies limit the improvement: the all-metrics superiority claim conflicts with Table 1, and Eq. 4 no longer matches its MSE description. Changed evaluation settings also prevent interpreting higher scores as demonstrated version-to-version gains.
